messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: KMS decrypt rate spike detected for project=redwood-prod, key=cmk-main (last 5m). 1.2k decrypts (baseline ~12). link: https://console.logging.example/alerts/9832

sara-sec: I see it. tagging oncall. @mike-oncall can you take command? this looks like a decrypt surge from svc-processor.

mike-oncall: on it. assigning roles: jordan = logs/timeline, lee = containment actions, i'll handle comms/escalation. ashley pls notify Product if customer-visible risk.

jordan-sre: pulling audit logs now. preliminary filter: "protoPayload.methodName=\"Decrypt\" AND resource.labels.project_id=\"redwood-prod\" AND timestamp>=\"2026-03-20T14:00:00Z\""

jordan-sre: snippet from logs (redacted):
```
principalEmail: svc-processor@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com
methodName: google.cloud.kms.v1.KeyManagementService.Decrypt
location: us-central1
requestCount: 1178
userAgent: python-requests/2.28
```

lee-devops: can we temporarily deny that service account decrypt permissions? Recommend revoke kms.cryptoKeyVersions.useToDecrypt on that SA or remove binding to roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter.

sara-sec: yes do that first. if we need to keep app up, we'll create fallback that routes to a degraded cached responses path. priority = contain exfil.

mike-oncall: lee, run the revoke now and post command/output. jordan keep collecting principals and target IPs.

lee-devops: running:
```
gcloud projects remove-iam-policy-binding redwood-prod --member=serviceAccount:svc-processor@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com --role=roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter
```

lee-devops: output: "Removed binding for svc-processor@..."

incident-bot: INCIDENT START: id=INC-20260320-01, severity=high, channel=#eng-oncall. Pager duty alerted.

mike-oncall: service account decrypt binding removed. prod request rate dropped to ~10/min within 90s. good containment signal.

jordan-sre: collected client IPs and request IDs, forwarding to secops bucket: gs://redwood-secops/incidents/INC-20260320-01/logs.tar.gz

sara-sec: next steps: 1) rotate CMK access material and create new key version, 2) rotate any SA keys that could be compromised, 3) audit RBAC bindings across projects for similar over-privileged SAs, 4) open follow-up ticket for postmortem and policy changes. Assign owners?

lee-devops: starting KMS key rotation (creating new key version)
```
gcloud kms keys create-rotation-schedule cmk-main --project=redwood-prod --location=us-central1 --keyring=prod-kr --rotation-period=30d
gcloud kms keys versions create --key=cmk-main --keyring=prod-kr --location=us-central1
```

lee-devops: new version created, staged. will schedule rewrap of any long-lived ciphertexts after approval.

mike-oncall: ashley please notify support+customers if there's any chance of impact. use the incident template: short statement, we detected anomalous KMS usage, contained, investigating, no confirmed data exfil at this time.

ashley-pm: support pinged. drafted note and waiting on sec confirmation before sending customer comms.

sara-sec: forensics: we need to snapshot svc-processor compute instances, collect container images and environment variables, and check CI/CD tokens used to deploy that SA. jordan add steps to timeline.

jordan-sre: done. timeline so far:
- 2109876543 ALERT: KMS decrypt spike detected
- +45s incident-bot auto-created incident
- +3m revoke IAM binding for svc-processor (lee)
- +4.5m decrypt rate returns to baseline
- +10m new KMS version created (lee)

sara-sec: containment verified. evidence archived. creating follow-up tickets:
- SEC-1234: RBAC least privilege audit (owner: sara-sec)
- INF-5678: KMS key rotation and rewrap play (owner: lee-devops)
- PM-8901: Customer comms review (owner: ashley-pm)

mike-oncall: closing actions for oncall: handoff to day team at +60m. please prepare short summary for morning standup.

ops-bot: Handoff reminder: escalation duty passed to day-oncall at 2109880143. Incident remains active (investigation).

sara-sec: thanks team. we'll run a deeper audit for similar SA patterns and a policy rule to prevent SAs with broad KMS bindings. leaving this thread open for updates.

mike-oncall: I'll write the incident timeline and draft the postmortem. tagging @ashley-pm and @lee-devops for owners on comms/rotation.

ashley-pm: ack. will coordinate support comms after sec sign-off.

lee-devops: I'll also add an automated alert rule to correlate KMS decrypt spikes with specific SA identities to reduce time to detect next time.

sara-sec: postmortem owners: lead = mike-oncall, sec analysis = sara-sec, infra remediation = lee-devops. target PMR (postmortem report) in 72h.

mike-oncall: noted. logging pointers and runbook links:
- runbook: https://wiki.redwood/internal/runbooks/kms-incident.md
- audit query used: https://console.logging.example/query?q=Decrypt+AND+redwood-prod

sara-sec: closing note for now: containment successful, evidence preserved, follow-ups created. will update when we have root cause. :lock:
